81157.subject: The ETHFI Buyback Catch
81157.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaa70932-7ce4-467e-b338-a662ed575d6a/0xR_NL_Banner_Heading_Wordmark.jpg?t=1776775276)
Caption: 

On our August 13th Analyst Hours call, I [explained](https://x.com/0xcarlosg/status/2088258500052812067?s=20) why I was bullish on ETHFI after the token had sold off due to the Ethereum staking proposal. The market was valuing EtherFi as a staking business, even though Cash, its neobank, was already generating the majority of protocol revenue. The missing piece was tokenholder value accrual. EtherFi’s investor call earlier that same day addressed it with programmatic buybacks starting in September, with the team providing initial guidance of about $1.33M a month.

Six weeks after launch, it’s worth checking how the program is tracking against that guidance, and why it can’t be compared with a typical buyback that takes tokens out of circulation.

Since the week of September 7, Labs has sent $1.48M to the Foundation to be used for buybacks, including another $225k yesterday, the third straight week at exactly that amount. Through October 18, the Foundation had bought 1.81M ETHFI at an average price of $0.692. At $225k a week, contributions are running at about $975K a month, roughly 27% below the $1.33M guidance.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/cc9151ac-252b-4636-94a8-3b4821c5ab78/image.png?t=1792488370)
Caption: 

The fixed $225k raises some questions, since the proposal was framed as if buybacks would scale directly with Cash spend. Over the past eight weeks, weekly Cash spend rose from $27.6M to $31.0M, yet contributions have stayed flat. If buybacks scaled directly with card spend, you would expect them to have increased, or at least fluctuated in value.

**Not your typical buyback**

Most token buybacks fall into one of two models. Buyback and burn, like PUMP or UNI, permanently removes tokens from supply. Buyback and retain, like Hyperliquid’s Assistance Fund, does not burn tokens but still takes them out of circulation. Either way, buybacks have the desired effect of shrinking the token’s float.

EtherFi’s buyback program works differently. The proposal said half of the ETHFI bought would be held in the Foundation treasury and half paid out as cashback. But based on the team’s [dashboard](https://dune.com/ether_fi/ethfi-buybacks), it looks like nearly all of it is going to cashback. EtherFi’s distributor contract has paid out 1.83M ETHFI over the past six weeks, basically everything that was bought. Recipients have since moved 1.28M of it, or 70%, out of their Cash accounts, and only 548k has been retained.

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/01d1f85e-a8d6-4a57-a372-839bf311bc29/image.png?t=1792488370)
Caption:

81070.subject: 💰 The Funding: What happens if MSCI drops crypto treasuries like Strategy?
81070.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c1c9af72-58d8-47c5-88eb-8e5007f7e3dc/unnamed__17_.png?t=1789144554)
Caption: 

Written by Yogita Khatri  | Edited by Zack Abrams

———————————————————————————

Presented By:

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0f002faa-88b1-4362-8467-fbc25a6c61ee/Screenshot_2026-10-16_at_4.02.56_PM__3___1___1___1_.png?t=1792184177)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

----------
Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 62nd edition of [The Funding](https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding)!

MSCI [finalized rules](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-15-msci-rules-could-exclude-strategy-mstr-from-indexes-418729) on Oct. 15 that could push Strategy and other crypto treasury companies out of its main global indexes as soon as Nov. 30. What would that mean for how these companies raise money, and is anyone still willing to fund them? I caught up with investors and analysts to find out.

Let's get into it.


----------———————————————————————————

----------
# THE INSIDE VIEW

## What if MSCI drops crypto treasuries?


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2012e140-bc90-4ae9-b029-9f403353161b/Dat-Image-1200x675.jpg?t=1792371900)
Caption: 

----------
Index provider MSCI recently [approved new rules](https://app2.msci.com/webapp/index_ann/DocGet?pub_key=aq0wbkjxPgo%3D&lang=en&format=html) that target "non-operating" companies, which mainly hold assets instead of running a business, such as digital asset treasury firms, or DATs.

Under the new rules, MSCI will first check whether a company has substantial operating assets, such as equipment or inventory. In the [proposal MSCI published in August](https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/indexes/consultations/equity/Consultation%20on%20Eligibility%20of%20Non-Operating%20Companies%20for%20the%20%20MSCI%20Global%20Investable%20Market%20Indexes.pdf), that meant operating assets making up more than half of total assets. Companies that fail this check face five financial tests, which in the proposal included whether a company generates operating cash flow and how much it relies on raising capital to buy assets. Those flagged on four or more will be excluded.

Current index members get some leeway: they will be removed only if they fail in both of their two most recent annual filing periods. If they fail in only one, they stay in the index unless they fail the following year. Companies not yet in the index are blocked if they fail in either of the last two years.

In a simulation published in August using May data, MSCI flagged two bitcoin treasury companies, Michael Saylor's Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet, for potential exclusion. Ethereum treasury firm SharpLink
